sourceChecks.location: Clay medium; wedge-shaped signs; Latin cuneus
sourceChecks.claim: Which ancient writing system takes its name from wedge-shaped signs? Answer: Cuneiform. In Mesopotamia, such signs were impressed into soft clay with a reed or wooden stylus. Adaptation: Global-MMLU, Cohere Labs et al., Apache 2.0.

reviewNotes: Met derives cuneiform from Latin wedge and describes reed/wood stylus signs in clay. Replaced source's disputed absolute 'earliest writing' assertion with a specific etymological fact. Hieroglyphs, Phoenician script and Linear B have different names; no mixed script/medium options.

sourceChecks.location: Old Kingdom: Snefru, founder of Fourth Dynasty; Khufu and Great Pyramid
sourceChecks.claim: For which pharaoh was the Great Pyramid at Giza built? Answer: Khufu (Cheops). It belongs to the Old Kingdom and the Fourth Dynasty.

reviewNotes: Cairo museum Old Kingdom section assigns Great Pyramid to Khufu, in Fourth Dynasty context. Djoser is linked to Saqqara and Snefru to Meidum/Dahshur; Ramesses II is a later pharaoh. Khufu/Cheops aliases share one option; RU/EN refer to the same Great Pyramid.

sourceChecks.claim: The famous Terracotta Army belongs to the burial complex of which ruler? Answer: Qin Shi Huang. He was the first emperor of the unified Qin state; unification is dated to 221 BC.
